b. Agranulocytes: i. These leucocytes are filled with non-granular and clear cytoplasm. ii. Nucleus is either round or kidney shaped which is comparatively larger sized.
iii. They comprise about 30% of total WBCs. iv. They are produced in lymphatic nodules.

Agranulocytes are of 2 types: • Lymphocytes: They are smaller cells with comparatively larger and spherical nucleus that nearly occupies the entire cell. They have small amount of cytoplasm. They produce antibodies. • Monocytes: They are large cells with kidney shaped nucleus. They have comparatively more cytoplasm. They are phagocytic.

Figure 8.4.23 Agranulocytes Functions of leucocytes or WBCs i. They destroy disease causing germs and have main role in the defensive mechanism of body. ii. They act as scavenger as they ingest harmful bacteria and other foreign particles and remove dead tissue cells. iii. They produce antibodies against different bacterial toxins. iv. Monocytes and neutrophil engulf the bacteria, dead cells and foreign particles. This is called phagocytosis or cell eating. v. Lymphocytes and eosinophil produce antitoxin to neutralize bacterial poison or toxin.

c. Platelets or Thrombocytes They are much smaller, nucleated and spindle shaped cells. They are colorless and produced in bone marrow. Their number is about 2-4 million per cubic mm and life span is of about 7 days.

Figure 8.4.24 Platelets Functions of Blood i. Transportation: Blood transport O2, CO2, glucose, amino acid, hormone, metabolic wastes to the target organs. ii. Regulation: Blood is the liquid medium transmitting uniform heat throughout body. It also controls level of water and salts in the body of frog. iii. Protection: WBCs protect the body from pathogenic bacteria viruses and other microbes by engulfing them and neutralizing their toxins. Clotting of blood occurs at the injured sites during excessive bleeding which is essential to save life. This is done by plasma protein and platelets.
